ev-be8f18ffe7.rationale: Maintainer decision of 2026-10-05 (ADR 0022; credential-evidence #64 and #65; a maintainer-only act, not reviewed, not independent validation): no outcome is asserted for this fixture. Not asserted: the token boundary. A well-formed Polar token with characters glued on or a body of another length is either a delimiter violation or a partially leaked token (ADR 0019 item 3), and no source decides it: Polar documents no delimiter rule, the contract claim field-boundary is unresolved, and the era-1 length is not stated by Polar. Whether a token must be delimited is one policy for every provider, not a Polar fact, so the fixture stays in the corpus unscored until that policy is decided. Earlier basis, kept for the record: project-policy, expected silence. Legacy tier T2 (tool-corroborated), but the cited sources do not include artifacts from two distinct owners, so the corroboration rule of docs/governance/evidence-classes.md is not met; the legacy expectation is recorded as project-policy pending review. ev-c1a673dc10.rationale: Polar's own server source (polarsource/polar @ 6a4f2f6) creates organization access tokens with generate_token_hash_pair(prefix="polar_oat_") (the one call site in the service; a development seed script calls the same helper): every token so created is the lower-case literal polar_oat_ followed by exactly 43 characters of [A-Za-z0-9] (37 random plus a 6-character base62 checksum). The organization access token was added after the generator took this form, so no earlier body shape applies. polar--polar-token-hyphen-in-body-twin has a hyphen inside the 43 characters after polar_oat_ (a run of 15, a hyphen, then a run of 27), and polar--polar-token-underscore-in-body-twin has an underscore inside them (a run of 20, an underscore, then a run of 22). The generator draws only from [A-Za-z0-9] and the base62 checksum digits, so neither value is a token Polar issued, and neither contains a run of 43 token characters. Negative twin of polar-token-json-api-key: alphabet: one body byte replaced by _, outside the era-2 [A-Za-z0-9]. Exactly one structural property differs from the positive; silence follows from construction. Read 2026-10-03 (raw files at the pinned commit; digests on the source observations). The step from the stated format to this value is a count or character test a reviewer can repeat; it is a statement about what Polar's code can issue, not about how any scanner should treat the value. Provider issuance, payload and checksum validity and liveness are not claimed.

sources.supports: generate_token(prefix) returns the prefix, then 37 characters drawn from string.ascii_letters + string.digits, then the CRC32 of those 37 characters as a 6-character base62 string (digits, upper-case, lower-case; zero-padded to 6): after the prefix, exactly 43 characters, each in [A-Za-z0-9].
generate_token_hash_pair(prefix=...) builds the token with generate_token(prefix=prefix).
TOKEN_PREFIX = "polar_oat_"
An organization access token is created with generate_token_hash_pair(prefix=TOKEN_PREFIX).
Commit 80fae7fc98 (author date 2025-01-02) replaces prefix + secrets.token_urlsafe(nbytes) in generate_token with 37 ascii_letters/digits plus a 6-character base62 CRC32.
Commit 4639cb7efd (author date 2025-02-04) adds organization access tokens with TOKEN_PREFIX = "polar_oat_" and generate_token_hash_pair(prefix=TOKEN_PREFIX), after the generator change above.

ev-polar-api-unknown-role.rationale: Polar's own server source (polarsource/polar @ 6a4f2f6) builds access-token and refresh-token prefixes from a two-entry map keyed by the two sub-types, which yields polar_at_u_, polar_at_o_, polar_rt_u_ and polar_rt_o_ and no other role letter. The value in polar--polar-api-credential-unknown-role-twin begins polar_rx_u_, which is not among them; a search of every file of the repository tree at the pinned commit (a tarball of that commit) finds no occurrence of the string polar_rx. So it is not a token prefix Polar's code produces. Negative twin of polar-api-credential-bearer-header: prefix: polar_rx_u_, a role the provider constants do not define. Exactly one structural property differs from the positive; silence follows from construction. Read 2026-10-03 (raw files at the pinned commit; digests on the source observations). This is a statement about what Polar's code issues at that commit, not about how any scanner should treat the value; the value's body length and alphabet are not relied on, and issuance, payload validity and liveness are not claimed.

sources.supports: ACCESS_TOKEN_PREFIX and REFRESH_TOKEN_PREFIX are dicts keyed by SubType whose values are exactly polar_at_u_, polar_at_o_, polar_rt_u_ and polar_rt_o_.

ev-polar-api-uppercase-prefix.rationale: Polar's own server source (polarsource/polar @ 6a4f2f6) defines the personal access token prefix as the lower-case literal polar_pat_ and prepends it unchanged when it mints a token. The value in polar--polar-api-credential-uppercase-prefix-twin begins POLAR_PAT_, which is not that literal, so it is not a token prefix Polar's code produces. Negative twin: prefix: POLAR_PAT_ vs the lower-case polar_pat_. Exactly one structural property differs from the positive; silence follows from construction. Read 2026-10-03. The personal access token service at the pinned commit holds the prefix constant only (it contains no token-minting call), so this entry relies on the constant and on the generator's prefix handling, not on a call site; it is not a statement about how any scanner should treat the value, and the body length and alphabet are not relied on.
